sentence: Waiting threads (the agent reported Waiting on a subagent or timer, or analysis found the work still in progress) rank after every other thread, even read ones.
context:
Heading: Sidebar (Workstreams thread list)
Previous paragraph: Read Waiting threads
Paragraph: Waiting threads (the agent reported Waiting on a subagent or timer, or analysis found the work still in progress) rank after every other thread, even read ones. Up Next then trims from the bottom: threads not blocked on you leave, least urgent first, until 5 remain; read blocked threads leave until 10 remain; past that, only the 10 most recently active stay, whatever their tier. So Up Next always shows a few threads, grows only for threads blocked on you, and lists at most 10 on its own. Show N more lists the trimmed threads that are unread or blocked on you below the rest, and Show less collapses them; trimmed read threads not blocked on you stay in Recent and their workstreams. It re-ranks as recaps, read state, and activity change. The thread you have open keeps its row and place until you open another thread. Nested delegates do not appear as separate Up Next entries; find them in their workstream's thread tree.

sentence: Limit and evidence: public experimental_serverAccess grants contain { id, serverUrl, headers? }, not a trusted core principal.
context:
Heading: Provider-neutral authenticated ingress for user-owned server access
Previous paragraph: Use case: a local plugin opens an outbound tunnel to a user-owned relay; a user-owned gateway authenticates individually scoped/revocable machine access without a hosted BB account, while BB/database remain local
Paragraph: Limit and evidence: public experimental_serverAccess grants contain { id, serverUrl, headers? }, not a trusted core principal. Public server.loopbackBaseUrl reaches ordinary trusted-localhost APIs. In request context and host enrollment, local enrollment-key minting and remote machine/gate identity are distinct. Proxying remote requests into loopback does not preserve that distinction. The newer SDK's internal_DO_NOT_USE_openTunnelIngress is explicitly Connect-only, and its implementation verifies Connect assertions and marks requests remote. No supported external plugin API attaches a provider-neutral principal or cross-checks an access grant's host against the native daemon/enrollment credential. Core removal can also skip provider release if the plugin is unavailable: cloud grant expiry/startup reconciliation cannot rely solely on lifecycle callbacks. Grants have no native credential-refresh callback. Stable provider credentials can avoid replacement, but worker reconfiguration after rotation must be demonstrated: enrolled bootstrap does not automatically deliver new headers

sentence: Workaround: Workstreams records unanswered questions in its own SQLite database before requesting native input.
context:
Heading: Preserve pending user questions across plugin reloads
Previous paragraph: Limit: plugin-runtime.ts unload calls pendingInteractions.interruptPluginInteractions(id), marking interactions plugin-disposed. Detached tool results are dropped. ui.requestInput offers neither a durable request ID nor a way for a new plugin generation to adopt the request and its waiter. The server log confirms questions dropped at exactly the reload timestamp. Removing the abort signal cannot prevent plugin-owned interaction disposal
Paragraph: Workaround: Workstreams records unanswered questions in its own SQLite database before requesting native input. The composer restores orphaned cards after reload, retains partial input in per-tab session storage, and delivers recovered answers through threads.send as ordinary user messages. Recap enforcement stands aside while the durable question remains unresolved. Native waiting status and original tool-call continuity are not preserved; the frontend disappears briefly while its bundle reloads. Recovered delivery claims the record before sending to prevent concurrent-tab duplicates, but the SDK offers no idempotency key: a crash or ambiguous network failure during send cannot guarantee exactly-once delivery. This is recovery, not transparent native interaction persistence

context:
Heading: Organization and categories
List introduction: Categories arrange rows inside a workstream without changing its topic, native section, or identity hue. Both the sidebar and phone Home show them. Previous paragraph: At 6 roots, the category classifier sees the whole collection and creates useful categories. It counts visible, non-archived, unsnoozed roots, including completed roots; delegates follow their root and do not count separately.
Paragraph: While categories exist, every arrival, departure, or substantive request that changes a root's work causes the classifier to reconsider the whole collection. Requests are assessed when dispatched, without waiting for Full analysis. It sees the current arrangement and should preserve it unless a change offers a meaningful organizational benefit. Cosmetic changes do not justify regrouping. There is no cooldown, periodic assessment, or separate incremental mode.

sentence: A topic holds threads or subtopics, never both.
context:
Heading: Core rules
Previous paragraph: Agent reports outrank fallback status. Structured questions (AskUserQuestion) and agent recaps (WorkstreamsRecap) take precedence over Full analysis for thread status, recap text, and needs you prompts. Full analysis supplies those fields only when the agent did not report.
Paragraph: A topic holds threads or subtopics, never both. Once a topic has subtopics, every thread in it is in one of them. Assignments, new subtopics, moves, and merges that would put threads beside subtopics are refused, whoever makes them; topic pickers list only topics without subtopics. Topic paths have at most two levels total. Adding children to a populated topic requires a reviewed filing plan for all stored assignments, including archived work, using meaningful lasting areas rather than a General or Other catch-all.

context:

Previous paragraph: Use the Sort workstreams menu to order workstreams by Name A–Z, Recent activity, or Manual order (drag headers within their tier).
Paragraph: Drag a root thread to another workstream to set its Topic to that workstream's topic; its delegates follow it. Drop on a row to place it before or after that root, or on a header to place it first, including a collapsed or recently emptied workstream. Drop in Unfiled to clear its topic. When the destination represents several topics, Workstreams uses the Placement model to choose an existing topic within that group. It shows Choosing a topic in the destination workstream… while choosing, then saves the choice as a manual topic.
